title: Vamadeva wakes: I am Brahman
hookLine: a seer wakes up and says: I was Manu, and the sun
carry: the self is Brahman, even now
tomorrow: one lesson that makes every other lesson make sense. real, or a scam?

lines: THE STORY IS WIDER THAN YOU.
I WAS MANU. I WAS THE SUN.
cards: The email arrives with a cheerful subject line: your ancestry results are in. A map lights up with places nobody at the family table ever mentioned.

All at once, the story of you is older and wider than the one you grew up with. In the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, a seer named Vamadeva goes much further than any map. He sits with one thought until it opens.
Then he says it out loud. I was Manu. I was the sun.
Is that a boast, a fever, or something else?

teach.h: IT KNEW ITSELF: I AM BRAHMAN.
teach.b: The passage tells it like a waking up. In the beginning, it says, this was Brahman, and it knew only its own self, the atman: I am Brahman. So it became all.
Then the circle widens. Whoever among the gods woke up to this became that. So too among the seers.
So too among people. Then one name. Seeing this, the seer Vamadeva understood: I was Manu, and the sun.
Manu, in the tradition, is the ancestor of humankind. So Vamadeva isn't puffing up one small life. He's speaking from past its edges: the whole human family, and the light that shines on all of it.
Look at who is on the list.

teach.h: I WAS MANU, AND THE SUN.
teach.b: The text doesn't say this happened once, to one special man, and then the door closed. It names him, and it names the door: knowing. Then come the two words that keep the passage from staying in the old days.
Even now. Even now, the text says, whoever knows I am Brahman becomes all this. Here is the teaching itself, plainly.
In the Upanishads, your deepest self, the atman, is not a small thing apart from Brahman, the one reality in everything. Waking up means knowing that.
Schools of Vedanta read aham brahmasmi in different ways, and the coming days give some of them a turn. This passage ends its part plainly. Even now.

how: In Vedanta study, the Brihadaranyaka's passage on Vamadeva is read with a teacher and a commentary, and aham brahmasmi is taught as one of the great sayings of the Upanishads.

o: I belong to Brahma, the god who creates
I am a god, set above other people
I am Brahman, the self known as the whole

games.q: the passage, piece by piece. tap the pairs.
p: it knew itself only: I am Brahman
I was Manu, and the sun
whoever knows it becomes all this

s: aham brahmasmi is one person bragging that he's God
the passage tells a waking up, open to gods, seers and people. schools read it differently; none reads it as a brag.
in the tradition, Manu is the ancestor of humankind
so 'I was Manu' reaches past one life to the whole human family.

games.q: a kid at camp says the old sages were basically superheroes, and none of that could happen to normal people now. what does this passage say?
o: right: the old sages had a power ordinary people don't have.
even now: whoever knows I am Brahman becomes all this.
it's only a story about the past, so it says nothing about now.
games.why: the passage lists gods, seers and people, names Vamadeva, then adds 'even now'. it doesn't lock the knowing in the past.

practice: Sit easy and let the breath find its own pace. On one out-breath, say two words softly, out loud if you can: even now. Then let them go, and listen to the quiet after them, which is also now.

wordCard.voice: Aham brahmasmi: I am Brahman. Vamadeva knew it as I was Manu, and the sun, and the text says the knowing still opens, even now.

orig.note: Sanskrit: I am Brahman. aham (I) + brahma (Brahman) + asmi (am), from the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.

carryVoice: Your line: the self is Brahman, even now. Eight days with aham brahmasmi, complete.

sources.ref: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.4.10 (in the beginning this was Brahman; it knew itself only: I am Brahman; so it became all; whoever among the gods, seers or people awoke to this became that; seeing this, the seer Vamadeva understood: I was Manu, and the sun; even now, whoever knows I am Brahman becomes all this)
